prediction.likelyOutcome: 7205 Telegraph has a strong liability case that the 2015 parking re-allocation breached the condominium instruments and violated the site plan's 30-space zoning minimum, aided by the undisclosed conflict of interest in the 2-0 board vote. The principal uncertainty is damages magnitude: expect the court to land somewhere between the Association's conservative diminution-in-value figure and 7205 Telegraph's appraiser's much larger figure, likely closer to the low-to-mid range given the credibility gap in O'Neill's assumptions, with lost-rent, over-assessment, and fee recoveries likely but currently unquantifiable on this record.

issues.label: Breach of condominium instruments / invalidity of 2015 parking re-allocation
Board self-dealing / undisclosed conflict of interest in the 2015 vote
Lost rent / lease termination damages from the D&K tenancy
Over-assessment of Phase I common element charges
Validity of the Association's November 2019 liens

outcome.description: After a bench trial the Fairfax County Circuit Court entered judgment for 7205 Telegraph on all four counts, awarding $481,434.84 in lost-rent contract damages, a further $6,296.70 for over-assessments, release of the association's liens, and $324,977.60 in attorney's fees and costs. A Court of Appeals panel affirmed on April 25, 2023; rehearing en banc was granted, and on December 19, 2023 the court lifted the stay and left the judgment affirmed.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed, including after rehearing en banc.
